items.prompt: For p=0.4 and a tiny positive b, why does the shown function check p*b <= 1-p before dividing by b?

options.text: The edge is nonpositive, so the required clamped output is already zero.
options.why: This branch avoids a needless large negative quotient while preserving the nonnegative-stake result.

options.text: Tiny positive odds always require the full stake.
options.why: Small payoff odds can make the edge unfavorable; they do not force fraction 1.

options.text: It changes the model to one with no possible loss.
options.why: The supplied p is unchanged. This is a computation branch, not a new probability model.

options.text: Division by any positive b is a syntax error in Python.
options.why: Positive floating division is allowed; the branch concerns bounded computation and the known zero result.
